newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slips as NYMEX WTI toys with $23.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slips as NYMEX WTI toys with $23.

text.p: IPE Brent crude slipped in afternoon trading as selling pressure built up on NYMEX crude which may test $23.00 a barrel support.
December Brent was down nine cents at $22.58 a barrel at 1547 GMT, just above the day's $22.50 low.
"The key support is $23 on NYMEX crude. Brent is following it down now but clearly failed to break to the upside today," said Alastair Harris of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.

In addition to weaker NYMEX futures, Brent has been dogged by soft physical crude markets. Cargoes of physical Brent are some 35 cents below December and the forward market shows little strength over the next month.
Harris pegged next support on Brent at the psychologically important level of $22 and on gas oil at $200 a tonne.
November gas oil was down $7 a tonne at $212 at 1552 GMT, having dipped to $211.25 earlier.
Dealers said oil markets had been thrown into confusion by the sharp losses incurred late on Thursday when fund selling hit prices hard.
In Europe the important gas oil to Brent spread has fallen this week, together with the differentials for physical oil.
Recent tightness for good quality 0.05 percent sulphur gas oil has been loosened and some banks were aggressively offering the spread between that and poorer quality grades.
"The banks seem to want to sell the November and December but keep length in the first quarter next year," said a swaps broker. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4948
